# Fact reference

What a check or a [policy pack](packs.md) can read: the facts the compiled-in collectors produce. A rule
names a fact by its path, for example `sshd.config.permitrootlogin.value`. `[]` stands for an element of a
list (`sshd.match[].criteria`, written with `over:` and an element variable in a `violations` check), `{}` for the
value under any key of a map (`sshd.config{}.value`, written `sshd.config.permitrootlogin.value` or
`sshd.config["permitrootlogin"].value` in a rule). A `setting` is a configuration value with `value`, `explicit`
and `source`; one that is not set and has no known default is absent from its map, so a rule that reads it
fails with `ERROR` instead of guessing. `vmsctl pack facts` prints the same names.

The fact types are the contract of rule authors, but before v1.0 they can change in a minor release.

## `accounts`

Accounts are the `accounts` facts: /etc/passwd and /etc/group.

| Path | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `accounts.users` | list of object |  |
| `accounts.users[].name` | string |  |
| `accounts.users[].uid` | int |  |
| `accounts.users[].gid` | int |  |
| `accounts.users[].home` | string |  |
| `accounts.users[].shell` | string |  |
| `accounts.users[].login_shell` | bool | LoginShell is false for nologin, false and similar shells. An empty shell field means /bin/sh, so it is a login shell. |
| `accounts.users[].password` | string | Password describes the password field of /etc/passwd itself: "shadowed" ("x"), "empty", "locked" ("*" or "!") or "hash" (a hash stored in the world-readable /etc/passwd). The value is never exposed. |
| `accounts.users[].source` | string |  |
| `accounts.groups` | list of object |  |
| `accounts.groups[].name` | string |  |
| `accounts.groups[].gid` | int |  |
| `accounts.groups[].members` | list of string |  |
| `accounts.groups[].source` | string |  |
| `accounts.duplicate_uids` | list of object | DuplicateUIDs are the UIDs shared by more than one account, so a check does not compare every account with every other (it would run out of its evaluation budget on a host with thousands of accounts). |
| `accounts.duplicate_uids[].uid` | int |  |
| `accounts.duplicate_uids[].users` | list of string | in /etc/passwd order |
| `accounts.duplicate_uids[].sources` | list of string | Sources are the /etc/passwd lines of Users, in the same order. |
| `accounts.empty_groups` | list of object | EmptyGroups are the groups with no members that are no account's primary group (computed here for the same reason as DuplicateUIDs). |
| `accounts.empty_groups[].name` | string |  |
| `accounts.empty_groups[].gid` | int |  |
| `accounts.empty_groups[].members` | list of string |  |
| `accounts.empty_groups[].source` | string |  |

## `audit`

Audit are the `audit` facts: the audit rules that the host loads at boot, read from the files, not from the running kernel
(a rule added with auditctl since boot is not seen; see the `services` facts for whether auditd starts). The files are
/etc/audit/rules.d/*.rules in name order, which is what augenrules merges into /etc/audit/audit.rules; /etc/audit/audit.rules
itself when there is no rules.d file. The keys of the rules (-k) are not kept: they are arbitrary names.

| Path | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `audit.present` | bool | Present is true when a rules file exists. |
| `audit.rules` | list of object | Rules are the rules of the files in the order they are loaded, with those that a later "-D" deleted left out. |
| `audit.rules[].kind` | string | Kind is "watch" (-w) or "syscall" (-a). |
| `audit.rules[].action` | string | Action and List are those of an -a rule ("always", "exit"); empty for a watch. |
| `audit.rules[].list` | string |  |
| `audit.rules[].path` | string | Path is the path of a watch, or the path= or dir= of an -a rule, without a trailing "/". |
| `audit.rules[].perms` | string | Perms are the audited permissions in the order r, w, a, x; of a watch without -p, all of them. |
| `audit.rules[].syscalls` | list of string | Syscalls are those of -S. |
| `audit.rules[].fields` | list of string | Fields are the other -F filters as written without spaces ("arch=b64", "auid>=1000"). |
| `audit.rules[].source` | string |  |
| `audit.paths` | map of object | Paths holds, for every path that a watch (-w) or an always,exit rule with path= and perm= audits, the permissions it audits (the union over the rules, in the order r, w, a, x: "wa", "x"), whoever the user is. A directory has no trailing "/". |
| `audit.paths{}.perms` | string |  |
| `audit.paths{}.source` | string | Source is the file and line of the first rule that audits it. |
| `audit.user_paths` | map of object | UserPaths is the same for the rules written for logged-in users: always,exit rules with path=, perm=, auid>=1000 and auid!=unset (also written -1 or 4294967295), the form that the STIG asks for the commands it names. |
| `audit.user_paths{}.perms` | string |  |
| `audit.user_paths{}.source` | string | Source is the file and line of the first rule that audits it. |

## `banner`

Banner is the `banner` facts: the texts shown before and after a login.

| Path | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `banner.files` | list of object |  |
| `banner.files[].path` | string |  |
| `banner.files[].exists` | bool | Exists is false when the file is missing. |
| `banner.files[].empty` | bool | Empty is true when the file has no text but white space. |
| `banner.files[].first` | string | First is the first line with text, cut to 100 characters. |
| `banner.files[].system_details` | list of string | SystemDetails lists the escapes getty expands into system details (\S the system name, \r the kernel release, \v the kernel version, \m the architecture, \s the OS name, \n the host name). |

## `bind`

Bind is the `bind` facts: who may transfer and update the zones BIND serves.
named.conf can hold TSIG keys, so its files are on the denylist and
hostfs.ReadBindConfig keeps no string from them.

| Path | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `bind.present` | bool | Present is false when there is no named.conf. |
| `bind.zones` | list of object | Zones are the primary and secondary zones, with what applies to each. |
| `bind.zones[].name` | string |  |
| `bind.zones[].type` | string | primary, master, secondary or slave |
| `bind.zones[].view` | string | "" outside a view |
| `bind.zones[].transfer` | string | Transfer is any (everyone may transfer the zone; BIND's default), restricted or none. |
| `bind.zones[].update` | string | Update is any, restricted (addresses, keys or an update-policy) or none (the default). |
| `bind.zones[].local` | bool | Local is true for the zones every installation defines for the host itself (localhost, 127.in-addr.arpa, ...). |
| `bind.zones[].where` | string |  |

## `filesystem`

Filesystem are the `filesystem` facts: files of concern found by walking
the target's local filesystems. Mounts of other kinds (pseudo filesystems
such as /proc, network shares, container storage) are not walked and are
listed in Excluded; a list is partial when the walk could not see
everything, so what it holds can fail a check but never make one pass.

| Path | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `filesystem.setid` | list of object | SetID are regular files with the set-user-ID or set-group-ID bit. |
| `filesystem.setid[].path` | string |  |
| `filesystem.setid[].type` | string | file, dir, symlink, socket, fifo, char, block |
| `filesystem.setid[].mode` | string | Mode is the permission and special bits in octal, e.g. "4755", "1777". |
| `filesystem.setid[].uid` | int |  |
| `filesystem.setid[].gid` | int |  |
| `filesystem.setid[].owner` | string | "" when the uid has no name |
| `filesystem.setid[].group` | string | "" when the gid has no name |
| `filesystem.world_writable` | list of object | WorldWritable are regular files and directories every user can write. |
| `filesystem.world_writable[].path` | string |  |
| `filesystem.world_writable[].type` | string | file, dir, symlink, socket, fifo, char, block |
| `filesystem.world_writable[].mode` | string | Mode is the permission and special bits in octal, e.g. "4755", "1777". |
| `filesystem.world_writable[].uid` | int |  |
| `filesystem.world_writable[].gid` | int |  |
| `filesystem.world_writable[].owner` | string | "" when the uid has no name |
| `filesystem.world_writable[].group` | string | "" when the gid has no name |
| `filesystem.unowned` | list of object | Unowned are entries whose owner or group has no name in /etc/passwd or /etc/group. |
| `filesystem.unowned[].path` | string |  |
| `filesystem.unowned[].type` | string | file, dir, symlink, socket, fifo, char, block |
| `filesystem.unowned[].mode` | string | Mode is the permission and special bits in octal, e.g. "4755", "1777". |
| `filesystem.unowned[].uid` | int |  |
| `filesystem.unowned[].gid` | int |  |
| `filesystem.unowned[].owner` | string | "" when the uid has no name |
| `filesystem.unowned[].group` | string | "" when the gid has no name |
| `filesystem.dev_files` | list of object | DevFiles are regular files under /dev (outside /dev/shm and /dev/mqueue), where only device nodes and directories belong. |
| `filesystem.dev_files[].path` | string |  |
| `filesystem.dev_files[].type` | string | file, dir, symlink, socket, fifo, char, block |
| `filesystem.dev_files[].mode` | string | Mode is the permission and special bits in octal, e.g. "4755", "1777". |
| `filesystem.dev_files[].uid` | int |  |
| `filesystem.dev_files[].gid` | int |  |
| `filesystem.dev_files[].owner` | string | "" when the uid has no name |
| `filesystem.dev_files[].group` | string | "" when the gid has no name |
| `filesystem.odd_names` | list of object | OddNames are files and directories whose name is only dots and spaces (other than "." and ".."), such as "..." or ". ": a way to hide a directory in a listing. |
| `filesystem.odd_names[].path` | string |  |
| `filesystem.odd_names[].type` | string | file, dir, symlink, socket, fifo, char, block |
| `filesystem.odd_names[].mode` | string | Mode is the permission and special bits in octal, e.g. "4755", "1777". |
| `filesystem.odd_names[].uid` | int |  |
| `filesystem.odd_names[].gid` | int |  |
| `filesystem.odd_names[].owner` | string | "" when the uid has no name |
| `filesystem.odd_names[].group` | string | "" when the gid has no name |
| `filesystem.log_files` | list of object | LogFiles are the files and directories under /var/log that root does not own. |
| `filesystem.log_files[].path` | string |  |
| `filesystem.log_files[].type` | string | file, dir, symlink, socket, fifo, char, block |
| `filesystem.log_files[].mode` | string | Mode is the permission and special bits in octal, e.g. "4755", "1777". |
| `filesystem.log_files[].uid` | int |  |
| `filesystem.log_files[].gid` | int |  |
| `filesystem.log_files[].owner` | string | "" when the uid has no name |
| `filesystem.log_files[].group` | string | "" when the gid has no name |
| `filesystem.excluded` | list of string | Excluded lists the mount points that were not walked, as "path (type)". |
| `filesystem.entries` | int | Entries is the number of entries the walk visited. |

## `firewall`

Firewall are the `firewall` facts: what the configuration of the host firewalls says, where the state of the unit is not
enough. ufw is the case: its unit is enabled by installing the package, while the firewall is on only when
/etc/ufw/ufw.conf says ENABLED=yes. (Whether a unit is enabled is in the `services` facts.)

| Path | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `firewall.ufw` | object |  |
| `firewall.ufw.present` | bool | Present is true when the file exists. |
| `firewall.ufw.settings` | map of setting | Settings has "enabled", the ENABLED of the file: "yes" or "no" (case and quotes do not matter); absent when the file does not set it. |
| `firewall.ufw.settings{}.value` | string | Value is the effective value as text. |
| `firewall.ufw.settings{}.explicit` | bool | Explicit is true when the value is set in a configuration file, false when it is a default. |
| `firewall.ufw.settings{}.source` | string | Source is where the value came from, e.g. "/etc/login.defs:25", "default (OpenSSH 9.6)" or "sshd -T". |

## `ftp`

FTP is the `ftp` facts: how vsftpd is configured. Other FTP servers are not
read.

| Path | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `ftp.present` | bool | Present is false when there is no vsftpd.conf. |
| `ftp.settings` | map of setting | Settings are the options the checks read: set in vsftpd.conf, or their built-in defaults (vsftpd.conf(5)). Booleans are YES or NO. |
| `ftp.settings{}.value` | string | Value is the effective value as text. |
| `ftp.settings{}.explicit` | bool | Explicit is true when the value is set in a configuration file, false when it is a default. |
| `ftp.settings{}.source` | string | Source is where the value came from, e.g. "/etc/login.defs:25", "default (OpenSSH 9.6)" or "sshd -T". |
| `ftp.banner` | string | Banner says what a client is told when it connects: "default" (the vsftpd banner, which names the version), "custom" or "version" (a custom banner, or banner_file, that still shows a version or the name vsftpd). |
| `ftp.root_denied` | bool | RootDenied is true when root cannot log in: the PAM stack of the FTP service refuses the users of a file that lists root (pam_listfile, /etc/ftpusers), or userlist_enable and userlist_deny make a listed root refused. |
| `ftp.root_denied_by` | string | RootDeniedBy is the file that lists root when RootDenied. |

## `homes`

Homes are the `homes` facts: the home directory of every account in
/etc/passwd and the shell startup files in it. Only metadata is read.

| Path | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `homes.accounts` | list of object |  |
| `homes.accounts[].user` | string |  |
| `homes.accounts[].uid` | int |  |
| `homes.accounts[].login_shell` | bool | LoginShell is the account's accounts.login_shell. |
| `homes.accounts[].path` | string |  |
| `homes.accounts[].exists` | bool | Exists is false when nothing is at Path (or Path is empty). |
| `homes.accounts[].owner_uid` | int | Owner and Mode describe Path (following a symbolic link) when it exists. |
| `homes.accounts[].mode` | string | octal, e.g. "0750" |
| `homes.accounts[].startup_files` | list of object | StartupFiles are the shell startup files present in the directory. |
| `homes.accounts[].startup_files[].path` | string |  |
| `homes.accounts[].startup_files[].uid` | int |  |
| `homes.accounts[].startup_files[].mode` | string |  |
| `homes.accounts[].startup_files[].dangling` | bool | Dangling is true for a symbolic link whose target does not exist: whoever creates the target controls the file. |

## `login_defs`

LoginDefs are the `login_defs` facts: /etc/login.defs (shadow-utils).

| Path | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `login_defs.present` | bool | Present is false when /etc/login.defs does not exist; the built-in defaults below still apply then. |
| `login_defs.settings` | map of setting | Settings are keyed by the exact (upper-case) key, e.g. PASS_MAX_DAYS. |
| `login_defs.settings{}.value` | string | Value is the effective value as text. |
| `login_defs.settings{}.explicit` | bool | Explicit is true when the value is set in a configuration file, false when it is a default. |
| `login_defs.settings{}.source` | string | Source is where the value came from, e.g. "/etc/login.defs:25", "default (OpenSSH 9.6)" or "sshd -T". |

## `mac`

MAC are the `mac` facts: the configuration of mandatory access control where a package or a unit alone does not say it. SELinux
is the case: the mode it starts in is the SELINUX of /etc/selinux/config. (AppArmor has no such file for it: it is on when its
package is installed and its unit is enabled, which are the `packages` and `services` facts.) The file says what the next boot
does, not what the running kernel does.

| Path | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `mac.selinux` | object |  |
| `mac.selinux.present` | bool | Present is true when the file exists. |
| `mac.selinux.settings` | map of setting | Settings has "mode", the SELINUX of the file ("enforcing", "permissive" or "disabled": case and quotes do not matter) and "type", its SELINUXTYPE ("targeted", "minimum", "mls"); a key the file does not set is absent. |
| `mac.selinux.settings{}.value` | string | Value is the effective value as text. |
| `mac.selinux.settings{}.explicit` | bool | Explicit is true when the value is set in a configuration file, false when it is a default. |
| `mac.selinux.settings{}.source` | string | Source is where the value came from, e.g. "/etc/login.defs:25", "default (OpenSSH 9.6)" or "sshd -T". |

## `nfs`

NFS is the `nfs` facts: /etc/exports and /etc/exports.d/*.exports. They
describe the static exports; an export added by a command at run time is not
in them.

| Path | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `nfs.present` | bool | Present is true when /etc/exports or a file in /etc/exports.d exists. |
| `nfs.exports` | list of object | Exports has one entry per client of each exported directory. |
| `nfs.exports[].path` | string |  |
| `nfs.exports[].client` | string | Client is the host, network, netgroup or wildcard the entry is for; "*" when the line names none (an export with only options is open to everyone). |
| `nfs.exports[].everyone` | bool | Everyone is true when the entry applies to every host: "*", or a client list that is only options. |
| `nfs.exports[].no_root_squash` | bool | NoRootSquash is true when the entry lets a remote root act as root. |
| `nfs.exports[].writable` | bool | Writable is true for rw (read-write is also allowed to be the default of no option: exports are read-only unless rw is given, as in exports(5)). |
| `nfs.exports[].where` | string |  |

## `packages`

Packages are the `packages` facts: what the package manager has installed.

| Path | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `packages.manager` | string | Manager is the package database the list comes from: "dpkg" or "rpm". |
| `packages.installed` | map of list of object | Installed maps a package name to its installed instances, in architecture order; a name has several on multi-arch systems. A package that is removed but has its configuration files left is not installed. |
| `packages.installed{}[].version` | string | Version is the full version: [epoch:]upstream[-revision] for dpkg, [epoch:]version-release for rpm. |
| `packages.installed{}[].arch` | string |  |
| `packages.installed{}[].state` | string | State is the dpkg status: "installed", or a partly installed state such as "unpacked" or "half-configured"; "installed" for rpm. |
| `packages.installed{}[].source` | string |  |

## `pam`

PAM are the `pam` facts: the PAM stacks of the services vmsctl checks and
the policies they enforce. Policies are decided here by evaluating each
stack the way libpam does (controls, jumps, substacks) for the situation
that matters, with each module's version-specific configuration, so rules
do not have to re-implement PAM.

| Path | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `pam.stacks` | map of list of object | Stacks maps a service (login, sshd, su, passwd) to its rules, with @include, include and substack expanded in place. A service without its own file gets the "other" stack, as PAM does. |
| `pam.stacks{}[].type` | string | auth, account, password or session |
| `pam.stacks{}[].control` | string | required, requisite, sufficient, optional or [...] |
| `pam.stacks{}[].module` | string | base name, e.g. pam_pwquality.so |
| `pam.stacks{}[].args` | list of string | Args are the module arguments; values of arguments that carry credentials (secret=, password=, key=, ...) and pam_exec's command are replaced by "<redacted>". |
| `pam.stacks{}[].source` | string |  |
| `pam.stacks{}[].scope` | string | Scope names the substack a rule came from ("" for the service's own stack): a sufficient or done result only ends its own scope. |
| `pam.password_quality` | object | PasswordQuality is the policy that rejects weak new passwords in the passwd service: pam_pwquality or pam_cracklib. Module is "" when no such module can reject a password (absent, ignored or skipped). |
| `pam.password_quality.module` | string |  |
| `pam.password_quality.settings` | map of setting |  |
| `pam.password_quality.settings{}.value` | string | Value is the effective value as text. |
| `pam.password_quality.settings{}.explicit` | bool | Explicit is true when the value is set in a configuration file, false when it is a default. |
| `pam.password_quality.settings{}.source` | string | Source is where the value came from, e.g. "/etc/login.defs:25", "default (OpenSSH 9.6)" or "sshd -T". |
| `pam.password_quality.ignored` | list of string | Ignored lists modules of this kind that are in the stack but cannot reject a password, with why (e.g. a sufficient rule ends the stack first). |
| `pam.password_history` | object | PasswordHistory is the policy that rejects reused passwords in the passwd service: pam_pwhistory, or pam_unix's remember option. |
| `pam.password_history.module` | string |  |
| `pam.password_history.settings` | map of setting |  |
| `pam.password_history.settings{}.value` | string | Value is the effective value as text. |
| `pam.password_history.settings{}.explicit` | bool | Explicit is true when the value is set in a configuration file, false when it is a default. |
| `pam.password_history.settings{}.source` | string | Source is where the value came from, e.g. "/etc/login.defs:25", "default (OpenSSH 9.6)" or "sshd -T". |
| `pam.password_history.ignored` | list of string | Ignored lists modules of this kind that are in the stack but cannot reject a password, with why (e.g. a sufficient rule ends the stack first). |
| `pam.lockout` | map of object | Lockout maps a service to the lockout policy of its auth stack. |
| `pam.lockout{}.module` | string | "" when neither is in the stack |
| `pam.lockout{}.settings` | map of setting |  |
| `pam.lockout{}.settings{}.value` | string | Value is the effective value as text. |
| `pam.lockout{}.settings{}.explicit` | bool | Explicit is true when the value is set in a configuration file, false when it is a default. |
| `pam.lockout{}.settings{}.source` | string | Source is where the value came from, e.g. "/etc/login.defs:25", "default (OpenSSH 9.6)" or "sshd -T". |
| `pam.lockout{}.actions` | list of string | Actions are the pam_faillock modes present: preauth, authfail and authsucc on auth lines, and account for an account line. |
| `pam.lockout{}.enforced` | bool | Enforced is true when the auth stack, evaluated as libpam does, counts a wrong password, denies a locked account even with the right password, and still lets an unlocked account in. |
| `pam.lockout{}.why` | string | Why says what is missing when Enforced is false. |
| `pam.effective` | map of setting | Effective holds what the stacks amount to. A key is absent when the stacks do not decide it: - su_wheel: "restricted" when the su stack denies a user outside the pam_wheel group who knows root's password; otherwise "not restricted: <why>". "restricted" also when every su found is restricted by its permissions: setuid root, a group of administrators (wheel, sudo, admin, adm), not executable by others. Absent when neither the su stack has a pam_wheel.so nor su is so restricted. - password_hash: the hash pam_unix in the passwd stack uses (md5, sha256, sha512, yescrypt, ...): its last hash option, or else the first ENCRYPT_METHOD of /etc/login.defs, which pam_unix reads. |
| `pam.effective{}.value` | string | Value is the effective value as text. |
| `pam.effective{}.explicit` | bool | Explicit is true when the value is set in a configuration file, false when it is a default. |
| `pam.effective{}.source` | string | Source is where the value came from, e.g. "/etc/login.defs:25", "default (OpenSSH 9.6)" or "sshd -T". |

## `postfix`

Postfix is the `postfix` facts: /etc/postfix/main.cf.

| Path | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `postfix.present` | bool | Present is false when /etc/postfix/main.cf does not exist. |
| `postfix.settings` | map of setting | Settings are the parameters set in main.cf (the last assignment wins, as in Postfix) and the defaults of the ones the checks read. |
| `postfix.settings{}.value` | string | Value is the effective value as text. |
| `postfix.settings{}.explicit` | bool | Explicit is true when the value is set in a configuration file, false when it is a default. |
| `postfix.settings{}.source` | string | Source is where the value came from, e.g. "/etc/login.defs:25", "default (OpenSSH 9.6)" or "sshd -T". |
| `postfix.relay_problems` | list of string | RelayProblems say why the configuration lets anyone relay mail through the server, one sentence each; empty when it does not. |

## `rsyslog`

Rsyslog is the `rsyslog` facts: the logging rules of /etc/rsyslog.conf and
the files it includes.

| Path | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `rsyslog.present` | bool | Present is false when there is no /etc/rsyslog.conf. |
| `rsyslog.rules` | list of object | Rules are the selector rules (auth,authpriv.* /var/log/auth.log). |
| `rsyslog.rules[].selector` | string |  |
| `rsyslog.rules[].target` | string | Target is a file, "@host" for a remote server, a legacy module action (":omusrmsg:", ":ommysql:": its arguments are dropped, they can hold a password), or the module of a RainerScript action. |
| `rsyslog.rules[].where` | string |  |

## `samba`

Samba is the `samba` facts: /etc/samba/smb.conf.

| Path | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `samba.present` | bool | Present is false when there is no smb.conf. |
| `samba.shares` | list of object | Shares are the shares ([global] and the special sections are not shares) and whether they allow guests. |
| `samba.shares[].name` | string |  |
| `samba.shares[].guest` | bool | Guest is true when the share is open to guests ("guest ok = yes" or "public = yes", on the share or as the default [global] had when the share began). |
| `samba.shares[].where` | string | Where is the line that opens the share to guests, or the share's own line. |

## `services`

Services are the `services` facts: which services are set up to start,
read from the files that decide it (unit files and their links, SysV init
links, inetd and xinetd configuration), so they are the same under --root;
and, on a live target, which systemd units are active.

Known gaps: units started only through Wants= or Requires= in other unit
files or drop-ins, and units that presets enable on a golden image's first
boot, do not show as enabled. On a live target, Active shows them if they
run.

| Path | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `services.systemd` | bool | Systemd is true when the target has systemd unit directories. |
| `services.active` | map of string | Active maps each unit systemd reports as active (or activating, reloading, ...) to its sub-state, such as "running", "listening" or "exited", on a live target. It is empty under --root and when systemd is not running; when systemd runs but cannot be asked, it is unknown. |
| `services.units` | map of object | Units maps a systemd unit name (ssh.service, telnet.socket, getty@tty1.service) to how it is set up. Every unit with a file or an enabling link is listed. |
| `services.units{}.enabled` | bool | Enabled is true when a .wants or .requires directory links to the unit, so it starts with the unit that wants it (at boot, for the usual targets). |
| `services.units{}.masked` | bool | Masked is true when the unit is linked to /dev/null or empty: it cannot start, enabled or not. |
| `services.units{}.file` | string | File is the unit file systemd loads (a template's for an instance), "" when there is none. |
| `services.units{}.alias_of` | string | AliasOf names the unit this name is an alias of, if it is one. |
| `services.units{}.exec` | string | Exec is the program of a service's first ExecStart= line in its unit file (drop-ins are not read), so a renamed unit is still recognized. |
| `services.units{}.source` | string | Source is the link that enables the unit, else its file. |
| `services.sysv` | map of object | SysV maps an /etc/init.d script to whether a boot runlevel starts it. systemd runs such scripts too, unless a unit of the same name exists. |
| `services.sysv{}.enabled` | bool | Enabled is true when an S link in /etc/rc[2-5S].d (or /etc/rc.d/rc[2-5].d) starts it. |
| `services.sysv{}.source` | string |  |
| `services.inetd` | list of object | Inetd lists the services /etc/inetd.conf starts (commented-out lines are not services). |
| `services.inetd[].name` | string |  |
| `services.inetd[].socket_type` | string |  |
| `services.inetd[].protocol` | string |  |
| `services.inetd[].user` | string |  |
| `services.inetd[].server` | string |  |
| `services.inetd[].args` | string |  |
| `services.inetd[].source` | string |  |
| `services.xinetd` | list of object | Xinetd lists the services of /etc/xinetd.conf and /etc/xinetd.d, enabled or not. |
| `services.xinetd[].name` | string |  |
| `services.xinetd[].disabled` | bool | Disabled is true when the service says disable = yes, or the defaults section disables it (its disabled list, or an enabled list without it). |
| `services.xinetd[].settings` | map of string | Settings are the section's other attributes (socket_type, protocol, user, server, only_from, ...), with += values appended. |
| `services.xinetd[].source` | string |  |
| `services.started` | list of object | Started lists everything above that starts a service: enabled units that are not masked, active units (live), enabled SysV scripts without a unit of the same name, inetd lines and enabled xinetd services. Checks for a service match it by name or program. It is partial when the active units are unknown. |
| `services.started[].service` | string | Service is the service's name without unit type or instance: "telnet" for telnet.socket, telnet@.service or an inetd telnet line. |
| `services.started[].name` | string | Name is the unit, script or inetd/xinetd service name. |
| `services.started[].kind` | string | unit, active, sysv, inetd or xinetd |
| `services.started[].program` | string | Program is the path of the program it runs, when known. |
| `services.started[].source` | string |  |

## `shadow`

Shadow are the `shadow` facts: the non-secret part of /etc/shadow.

| Path | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `shadow.present` | bool | Present is false when /etc/shadow does not exist. |
| `shadow.entries` | list of object |  |
| `shadow.entries[].name` | string |  |
| `shadow.entries[].state` | string | State is "set", "locked" or "empty" (no password). |
| `shadow.entries[].algorithm` | string | Algorithm is the hash algorithm (yescrypt, sha512, sha256, bcrypt, md5, des, ...), or "" without a hash. |
| `shadow.entries[].last_change` | int | Aging fields in days; -1 when empty. |
| `shadow.entries[].min_days` | int |  |
| `shadow.entries[].max_days` | int |  |
| `shadow.entries[].warn_days` | int |  |
| `shadow.entries[].inactive_days` | int |  |
| `shadow.entries[].expire` | int |  |
| `shadow.entries[].source` | string |  |

## `shell_env`

ShellEnv are the `shell_env` facts: what root's bash login shell sets,
following the files it reads in order: /etc/environment (pam_env), then
/etc/profile and the first of ~/.bash_profile, ~/.bash_login and
~/.profile, and the files they source (/etc/profile.d/*.sh, sh.local,
bashrc files). Shell scripts cannot be evaluated statically, so every
occurrence is listed in reading order, marked conditional when it may not
run (inside if, case, loops, functions or subshells, or after && or ||);
rules decide what to accept.

| Path | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `shell_env.tmout` | list of object | TMOUT assignments and unsets |
| `shell_env.tmout[].value` | string |  |
| `shell_env.tmout[].readonly` | bool | readonly or declare -r on the same command |
| `shell_env.tmout[].conditional` | bool | may not run; see ShellEnv |
| `shell_env.tmout[].unset` | bool | an unset command (TMOUT only); Value is "" |
| `shell_env.tmout[].source` | string |  |
| `shell_env.umask` | list of object | umask commands |
| `shell_env.umask[].value` | string |  |
| `shell_env.umask[].readonly` | bool | readonly or declare -r on the same command |
| `shell_env.umask[].conditional` | bool | may not run; see ShellEnv |
| `shell_env.umask[].unset` | bool | an unset command (TMOUT only); Value is "" |
| `shell_env.umask[].source` | string |  |
| `shell_env.path` | list of object | PATH assignments |
| `shell_env.path[].value` | string |  |
| `shell_env.path[].readonly` | bool | readonly or declare -r on the same command |
| `shell_env.path[].conditional` | bool | may not run; see ShellEnv |
| `shell_env.path[].unset` | bool | an unset command (TMOUT only); Value is "" |
| `shell_env.path[].source` | string |  |
| `shell_env.effective` | map of setting | Effective maps a variable to what its unconditional assignments and unsets leave, in reading order (once it is read-only, later changes fail). A variable is absent when no value survives. The map is unknown when a conditional change could alter the result. Only TMOUT is tracked. |
| `shell_env.effective{}.value` | string | Value is the effective value as text. |
| `shell_env.effective{}.explicit` | bool | Explicit is true when the value is set in a configuration file, false when it is a default. |
| `shell_env.effective{}.source` | string | Source is where the value came from, e.g. "/etc/login.defs:25", "default (OpenSSH 9.6)" or "sshd -T". |
| `shell_env.system_effective` | map of setting | SystemEffective is the same for the system-wide files only (/etc/environment, /etc/profile and what it sources): what every user's login shell gets, before their own startup files. |
| `shell_env.system_effective{}.value` | string | Value is the effective value as text. |
| `shell_env.system_effective{}.explicit` | bool | Explicit is true when the value is set in a configuration file, false when it is a default. |
| `shell_env.system_effective{}.source` | string | Source is where the value came from, e.g. "/etc/login.defs:25", "default (OpenSSH 9.6)" or "sshd -T". |

## `snmp`

SNMP is the `snmp` facts: how the net-snmp agent is configured to be reached.
A community string is a password: the configuration files are on the denylist
and hostfs.ReadSNMPConfig keeps only what can be said without the string
(whether it is a well-known name or short, which source it answers).

| Path | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `snmp.present` | bool | Present is false when none of the agent's configuration files exists. |
| `snmp.communities` | list of object | Communities are the SNMPv1 and v2c access entries: rocommunity, rwcommunity, authcommunity and com2sec lines. |
| `snmp.communities[].directive` | string | Directive is the configuration keyword (rocommunity, com2sec, ...). |
| `snmp.communities[].weak` | string | Weak says why the string is easy to guess: "a well-known name" or "shorter than 8 characters"; "" when it is neither. |
| `snmp.communities[].unrestricted` | bool | Unrestricted is true when the entry answers every source address. |
| `snmp.communities[].source` | string | Source is the address the entry is limited to, "" for none. |
| `snmp.communities[].where` | string | Where is file:line. |
| `snmp.listen` | list of string | Listen are the agentAddress addresses, as written; empty when the files do not set them (the agent then listens on every interface). A listen address given on the command line overrides them and is not seen here. |
| `snmp.loopback_only` | bool | LoopbackOnly is true when agentAddress is set and every address is a loopback address. |

## `sockets`

Sockets are the `sockets` facts: the TCP and UDP sockets of the running
system that accept traffic, from /proc/net. Which program owns a socket is
not recorded, and a port alone does not identify a service (RPC services
get theirs from rpcbind): checks combine sockets with other signals.

| Path | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `sockets.listening` | list of object |  |
| `sockets.listening[].protocol` | string | tcp or udp |
| `sockets.listening[].address` | string | local address: 0.0.0.0, ::, 127.0.0.1, ... |
| `sockets.listening[].port` | int |  |
| `sockets.listening[].loopback` | bool | Loopback is true when only the host itself can reach the socket. |
| `sockets.listening[].uid` | int |  |
| `sockets.listening[].source` | string |  |

## `sshd`

SSHD are the `sshd` facts: the OpenSSH server configuration.

| Path | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `sshd.present` | bool | Present is true when an sshd program or its configuration exists. |
| `sshd.config` | map of setting | Config holds the effective global settings, keyed by lowercase keyword. On a live host the values come from `sshd -T`, so defaults of the installed version are included (explicit=false); otherwise only values set in the files are known. |
| `sshd.config{}.value` | string | Value is the effective value as text. |
| `sshd.config{}.explicit` | bool | Explicit is true when the value is set in a configuration file, false when it is a default. |
| `sshd.config{}.source` | string | Source is where the value came from, e.g. "/etc/login.defs:25", "default (OpenSSH 9.6)" or "sshd -T". |
| `sshd.match` | list of object | Match lists the Match blocks, whose settings override the global ones for matching connections. |
| `sshd.match[].criteria` | string |  |
| `sshd.match[].settings` | map of setting |  |
| `sshd.match[].settings{}.value` | string | Value is the effective value as text. |
| `sshd.match[].settings{}.explicit` | bool | Explicit is true when the value is set in a configuration file, false when it is a default. |
| `sshd.match[].settings{}.source` | string | Source is where the value came from, e.g. "/etc/login.defs:25", "default (OpenSSH 9.6)" or "sshd -T". |
| `sshd.match[].source` | string |  |

## `sysctl`

Sysctl are the `sysctl` facts: the kernel parameters that checks read (sysctlKeys, not every parameter).

| Path | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `sysctl.live` | bool | Live is true when the values are what the running kernel reports (/proc/sys). Otherwise they are what the configuration files set at boot, and a parameter they do not set is absent: the kernel's own default is not known. A container image shares the kernel of its host, so it has no values at all (the checks do not apply to it). |
| `sysctl.params` | map of setting | Params are keyed by the parameter's name with dots, e.g. kernel.kptr_restrict. |
| `sysctl.params{}.value` | string | Value is the effective value as text. |
| `sysctl.params{}.explicit` | bool | Explicit is true when the value is set in a configuration file, false when it is a default. |
| `sysctl.params{}.source` | string | Source is where the value came from, e.g. "/etc/login.defs:25", "default (OpenSSH 9.6)" or "sshd -T". |

## `target`

Target describes what is being scanned: the `target` variable.

| Path | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `target.live` | bool | Live is true when the target is the running system, so live facts (running services, sockets) describe it; false for a mounted root (--root), where nothing runs. Checks use it to require live facts on live targets only. |
| `target.image` | bool | Image is true when the target is a container image (--image-tar): its files, with nothing running and no kernel of its own. Checks of kernel parameters do not apply to it. |

## `updates`

Updates are the `updates` facts: the configuration of the tools that install updates by themselves. Whether their units
(timers, services) are enabled is in the `services` facts, and whether a package is installed in `packages`.

| Path | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `updates.apt` | object | Apt is what apt's configuration says about periodic runs (unattended-upgrades). |
| `updates.apt.present` | bool | Present is true when a file of the apt configuration directory or /etc/apt/apt.conf exists. |
| `updates.apt.settings` | map of setting | Settings has "enable", "update_package_lists" and "unattended_upgrade" (APT::Periodic::Enable and so on). |
| `updates.apt.settings{}.value` | string | Value is the effective value as text. |
| `updates.apt.settings{}.explicit` | bool | Explicit is true when the value is set in a configuration file, false when it is a default. |
| `updates.apt.settings{}.source` | string | Source is where the value came from, e.g. "/etc/login.defs:25", "default (OpenSSH 9.6)" or "sshd -T". |
| `updates.dnf_automatic` | object | Dnf is /etc/dnf/automatic.conf (dnf-automatic) and Yum is /etc/yum/yum-cron.conf (yum-cron). |
| `updates.dnf_automatic.present` | bool |  |
| `updates.dnf_automatic.settings` | map of setting | Settings has "apply_updates", "yes" or "no" (yes, true, on and 1 are yes; the other spellings of no are no), and "upgrade_type", what is installed: "security" or "default" (everything); for yum-cron it is update_cmd, which has the same usual values. |
| `updates.dnf_automatic.settings{}.value` | string | Value is the effective value as text. |
| `updates.dnf_automatic.settings{}.explicit` | bool | Explicit is true when the value is set in a configuration file, false when it is a default. |
| `updates.dnf_automatic.settings{}.source` | string | Source is where the value came from, e.g. "/etc/login.defs:25", "default (OpenSSH 9.6)" or "sshd -T". |
| `updates.yum_cron` | object |  |
| `updates.yum_cron.present` | bool |  |
| `updates.yum_cron.settings` | map of setting | Settings has "apply_updates", "yes" or "no" (yes, true, on and 1 are yes; the other spellings of no are no), and "upgrade_type", what is installed: "security" or "default" (everything); for yum-cron it is update_cmd, which has the same usual values. |
| `updates.yum_cron.settings{}.value` | string | Value is the effective value as text. |
| `updates.yum_cron.settings{}.explicit` | bool | Explicit is true when the value is set in a configuration file, false when it is a default. |
| `updates.yum_cron.settings{}.source` | string | Source is where the value came from, e.g. "/etc/login.defs:25", "default (OpenSSH 9.6)" or "sshd -T". |
